'''Donna Jean Brogan''' (born July 12, 1939) is an American [[statistician]] and [[Emeritus|professor emeritus]] of [[statistics]] at [[Emory University]]. Brogan has worked in biostatistical research in the areas of women's health, mental health and [[psychosocial]] health statistics, statistics on breast cancer, and analysis of complex survey data.

== Early life and education ==
Brogan was born July 12, 1939, and grew up in a working-class neighborhood in [[Baltimore]], Maryland, and she was the first in her family to go to college.<ref name="CHANCE">{{cite web|url=http://chance.amstat.org/2017/04/womenrise/|title=Challenging Sex Discrimination: Reflections over Seven Decades|publisher=American Statistical Association|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170920005618/http://chance.amstat.org/2017/04/womenrise/|archive-date=20 September 2017}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://plaza.las.iastate.edu/directory/donna-ruhl-brogan/|title=Donna Ruhl Brogan -|website=Plaza of Heroines, Iowa State University|language=en|access-date=2018-11-21}}</ref> She earned a B.A. in mathematics from [[Gettysburg College]] in 1960, an M.S. in statistics from [[Purdue University]] in 1962.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://www.stat.purdue.edu/alumni/distinguished_alumni/brogan-96.html|title=1996 Distinguished Alumna Donna Brogan|date=1996|website=Purdue University - Department of Statistics|language=en|access-date=2018-11-21}}</ref> She earned a PhD in statistics from [[Iowa State University]] in 1967,<ref name=":0" /> under the supervision of Joseph Sendransk.

== Work ==
In 1971, Brogan founded the [[Caucus for Women in Statistics]], and helped to establish the standing ASA Committee on Women in Statistics.<ref name="DBroganCV">{{cite web|url=https://www.sph.emory.edu/faculty/profile/#!DBROGAN|title=Donna Brogan|publisher=Rollins School of Public Health, Emory University}}</ref>

For four years, she was an assistant professor in the [[University of North Carolina]] in the School of Public Health, with a specialization in sample survey design and analysis. Then in 1970, she joined the [[Emory University School of Medicine]] as associate professor, later professor in the Department of Statistics and Biometry.<ref name=":2">{{Cite news|url=https://www.sph.emory.edu/departments/bios/calendar/brogan-lecture/index.html|title=Donna J. Brogan Lecture in Biostatistics|work=Emory University|access-date=2018-11-21}}</ref> Between 1991 and 1994, she was the division director of biostatistics at Emory.<ref name=":1" /> She retired in 2004 from Emory University.<ref name=":2" />

Since 1975, she has worked in freelance and active as a biostatistician, primarily in the specialty area of design and analysis of complex sample surveys.

== Personal life ==
As a woman in mathematics in the 1950s and 1960s, she suffered from many incidents of sex discrimination, including issues with unequal compensation from the [[University of North Carolina Chapel Hill]] and [[Emory University]], as well as a legal battle with the [[DeKalb County, Georgia|DeKalb County]] voter registrar, which involved the [[American Civil Liberties Union]].<ref name="CHANCE" />

She was married to {{ill|Charles Ruhl|sv}}, and had two children, although their son died in infancy.<ref name="CHANCE" /> Brogan and Ruhl later divorced, and Brogan lived as a single mother for several years.

== Awards and honors ==
She is a [[List of Fellows of the American Statistical Association#1985|Fellow]] of the [[American Statistical Association]], received the Emory University Thomas Jefferson Award from Emory University  in 1993,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://provost.emory.edu/awards/university/jefferson.html|title=Emory University Thomas Jefferson Awardees|publisher=Emory University|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171014170430/http://provost.emory.edu/awards/university/jefferson.html|archive-date=14 October 2017}}</ref> and was awarded the Iowa State University Distinguished Alumni Award in 2002.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.isualum.org/pride/awards/distinguished-awards-celebration/distinguished-alumni-award/|title=Iowa State University Distinguished Alumni Award|publisher=Iowa State University|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170402170448/http://www.isualum.org/pride/awards/distinguished-awards-celebration/distinguished-alumni-award/|archive-date=2 April 2017}}</ref> In 1995, Iowa State University engraved her name on its ''Plaza of Heroines'', which honors outstanding women graduates and faculty.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

The "Donna J. Brogan Lecture in Biostatistics" was established in 2004 at Emory University, to honor Brogan's work at the school.<ref name=":2" />
